title: Your Groceries Just Got Pricier: India's Inflation Crosses RBI's Target
description: India's retail inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), rose to 4.38% in June 2026. This is the first time in 16-17 months that inflation has go.

faq.a: It means that the measured retail inflation rate for June 2026 (4.38%) has gone above the 4% midpoint target that the Reserve Bank of India aims for, indicating that prices are rising faster than the central bank prefers.

faq.q: Will this definitely lead to an interest rate hike?
faq.a: Not necessarily immediately, but it increases the likelihood. The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will closely watch future inflation data and other economic indicators before deciding whether to raise interest rates to cool down price increases.

faq.q: Why are food and fuel prices so important for India's inflation?
faq.a: Food and fuel make up a large portion of the average Indian household's expenses. When their prices rise, it quickly impacts the overall cost of living for most people, leading to a significant increase in the headline inflation number.

faq.q: How often is India's CPI data released?
faq.a: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) releases the CPI data every month, usually around the middle of the following month.

faq.q: What is the difference between retail and wholesale inflation?
faq.a: Retail inflation (CPI) measures price changes at the consumer level, reflecting what you pay for goods and services. Wholesale inflation (WPI) measures price changes at the producer or wholesale level, before goods reach the consumer. CPI is generally more relevant for household budgets.
